fields.meta_title: IT Automation for Internal IT Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See four IT automation examples an internal IT team runs: software requests, laptop refresh, update reminders, and renewals. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build IT Automation for the Requests Your IT Team Repeats
fields.hero_description: Build IT automation that approves software requests, flags aging laptops, and chases overdue updates for your IT team.
fields.features_heading: The Request and Tracking Work IT Does by Hand
fields.features_subheading: IT automation is the use of software to perform repetitive IT tasks with reduced human assistance, built around the tools you pay for.
fields.feature_1:
Request rules you write as sentences

You describe who can ask for what and who signs off, in plain English. Emergent builds the request form, approval logic, and database, and you change a rule by prompting.
fields.feature_2:
Connected to the admin tools you pay for

The app reads from and writes to any tool with an API, such as a device management console or a software admin panel. A seat added in the app shows up in that tool's own list.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders sent to the person who can act

Overdue updates and requests that sit too long each trigger an alert in Slack, by email, or in the app. You choose who gets it and when a reminder escalates to the IT lead.
fields.feature_4:
An asset list that stays current

Each laptop, its owner, its purchase date, and its update status sit in one database you own. The dashboard updates live, showing overdue devices and waiting requests.
fields.feature_5:
No task cap during a busy quarter

A hiring wave can double a week of software requests and laptop orders. Emergent sets no task cap on automation, and every extra run in that week keeps going as normal.
fields.feature_6:
The code goes to your GitHub repository

On paid plans, Emergent exports the app's full code, every rule included, to your GitHub repository. Anyone who reads code can check how each request gets approved or held.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Jobs IT Can Stop Doing by Hand
fields.tab_content_1:
Seats under $25 a month need no sign-off

Linnea Vrabel asks for a seat in the team whiteboard app, which costs $12 a month. Requests under $25 a month are approved without review. The app adds her seat through the whiteboard app's admin API and messages Linnea that it is ready. A pricier request would wait for the IT manager instead.
fields.tab_content_2:
A replacement request for every laptop at 48 months

Teodor Beaumont's laptop, L-0417, has reached 48 months in service. The app reads its age from the asset list, opens replacement request R-1182, and adds L-0417 to the Q4 purchase list. Younger laptops in the list stay as they are.
fields.tab_content_3:
Fifteen days late, the update reaches its owner

The device management tool reports that Saoirse Kettunen's laptop, L-0388, has gone 15 days without a security update. Your limit is 14 days. The app sends Saoirse a direct message asking her to install the update and restart, and marks L-0388 overdue on the IT dashboard.
fields.tab_content_4:
38 of 150 seats sat unused before the renewal

The project tracker contract renews in 30 days with 150 paid seats, and only 112 people signed in during the last 60 days. The app sends Dag Holmqvist, the IT manager, a renewal summary of the 38 unused seats with a Review seats button, before anyone signs.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to choose the IT automation worth building first, write its rules, and test it on real requests before launch.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put a number on every rule
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 List the system that owns each fact
fields.howto_step_1_des: Export last quarter's help desk tickets and group them by request type. Mark the types that end the same way every time, such as a seat added or a laptop ordered. Automate those first.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Swap judgment words for limits the app can test. Write "under $25 a month", not "cheap", and "14 days late", not "overdue for a while". A rule with a number can run without anyone reading it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Note where each answer lives: purchase dates in the asset list, update status in the device management tool, seat counts in each admin panel. Read from that system, never from a spreadsheet copy.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write the request form, the rules, and who hears about each exception in one prompt. Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard, and connects to each of your tools through its API.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give every alert a person, not a shared inbox. Pick who answers an overdue update, who signs off on a costly request, and who reviews a renewal, and name a backup for each one's vacation.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last month's requests through the app before it touches a live account. Check that each was approved, held, or flagged the way your team handled it by hand, and fix any rule that disagrees.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Switch on the read-only parts first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Start with the automations that only read and remind, such as aging laptops and overdue updates. After two weeks without a wrong alert, turn on the ones that add seats or open purchase requests.

faq_plan.q: What is IT automation with Python?
faq_plan.ref: what is it automation with python
faq_plan.a: It means writing Python scripts that do IT tasks a person would otherwise repeat by hand, such as creating accounts or checking disk space. At its core, IT automation involves running scripts that define and execute a sequence of specific actions. Those actions can be triggered manually, on a set schedule, or by specific events.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up IT automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick one routine request, such as a software seat, and describe it in Emergent's AI automation builder: who asks, the limit that decides it, and who hears about the exceptions. The free tier covers building and publishing that first app. Once it runs, add the next request type to the same app with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What is IT automation software integration?
faq_plan.ref: what is it automation software integration
faq_plan.a: It is the connection between your automation software and the systems IT already runs, which lets a step in one tool start work in another. A new hire added in the HR system can start an account request, and an approved seat can be written straight to an app's admin panel. Apps built with Emergent connect this way to your HR system and admin panels through their APIs.

IT process automation runs a whole IT process end to end, not a single task. A request comes in and is checked against a rule; then it is carried out and logged. Resetting one password is a task; handling every access request from the form to the audit trail is a process. Outages follow a process of their own, covered by incident response automation.

faq_plan.q: What do IT automation tools do?
faq_plan.a: IT automation tools run repeat IT work when a trigger fires or a schedule comes due, and record what they did. Before you compare names, decide which kind of work you need covered. Some tools configure servers and networks from code, and others handle the requests and records around people, such as software seats and laptops.

faq_plan.q: When are IT automation services worth paying for?
faq_plan.a: They are worth it when the work needs skills your team lacks, such as scripting a change across hundreds of servers, or when nobody has time to own the build. Before you sign, ask who will change a rule next year and what that costs. In an app built with Emergent, a rule changes when someone on your team prompts for the new one.

faq_plan.q: Do IT automation solutions replace the help desk?
faq_plan.a: No. They take the routine requests that a fixed rule can decide, and the help desk keeps the ones that need a conversation, like a cracked screen or an unusual access request. A single scheduled step with no request behind it, such as a weekly report email, is task automation, not IT work.

IT infrastructure automation sets up and changes servers, cloud environments, and networking components without manual steps. Provisioning is the process of setting up that infrastructure. Infrastructure as code automates it with a high-level descriptive coding language. Keep those files in version control and review each change the way you would review application code.

faq_plan.q: What does IT operations automation cover?
faq_plan.a: IT operations automation covers the daily run work that keeps systems healthy: applying patches, confirming that backups finished, and answering monitoring alerts. Give each check a pass condition you can write down, such as a backup that finished before 6 a.m. Emergent-built apps keep every result in a database you own, ready for a monthly review.

faq_plan.q: How does IT workflow automation pass work to finance?
faq_plan.a: It passes work through a record finance already uses. A laptop replacement leaves IT as a purchase request, and from there it follows your purchase order automation through approval and ordering. Agree on the fields that travel with each handoff, such as the asset tag and the owner, before you build it.

plan.angle: The top 10 are vendor and course explainers that define IT automation in the abstract and stop at server scripts and infrastructure as code. This page shows the request-and-tracking side an internal IT team actually runs every week, drawn as working screens: a $12 software seat approved under a $25 limit, a laptop flagged at 48 months, an overdue security update chased with the laptop's owner, and a contract renewal that shows 38 unused seats before anyone signs. The FAQ covers the definitions searchers compare: Python scripts, process, infrastructure, operations, tools and services.
